retrieval_method: Europe PMC REST core record for EXT_ID:31551155 (confirmed Fertil Steril 2019;112(6):1071-1079.e7), then parallel-cli extract --full-content of the fertstert.org full-text page. I did NOT use any file in figs_source/.
quote_found: All patients with an ongoing pregnancy at 20 weeks' gestation continued to a live birth. Thus, the OPR at 20 weeks also reflects the live birth rate in this study cohort. The overall OPRs per transfer at 20 weeks' gestation was not significantly different between the PGT-A and control arms for either the embryo transfer population (50.0% [137/274] vs. 45.7% [143/313]; P=.32) or the ITT population (41.8% [138/330] vs. 43.5% [144/331]; P=.65).
what_is_wrong: Nothing material. I attacked all four components and each held. (a) Quote is verbatim. (b) Table 3 row read directly: 'Ongoing pregnancy at 20 weeks' gestation |75 (49.3) |89 (53.0) |62 (50.8) |54 (37.2) |137 (50.0) |143 (45.7) |.3177' under headers 'PGT-A (n = 274) |Control (n = 313)' - so the claimed P=.3177 comes from Table 3 (the Results text rounds it to P=.32), exactly as the claim states. (c) Freezing held constant in both arms: 'to undergo an IVF cycle with the intent to receive a single embryo transfer (SET) after vitrification and subsequent warming' and Discussion 'select euploid embryos for single vitrified-warmed blastocyst transfer'. (d) Inclusion criterion verbatim: 'female age 25-40 years undergoing IVF with autologous oocytes with at least two blastocysts of sufficient quality for biopsy and vitrification by day 6'. My own arithmetic: 137/274=50.00%, 143/313=45.69%, RD=+4.31pp, matching the claimed +4.3.

retrieval_method: Same parallel-cli extract of the fertstert.org full text; the quoted sentence sits in the authors' own structured abstract (Result(s)) of that page.
quote_found: The OPR was equivalent between the two arms, with no significant difference per embryo transfer (50% [137/274] vs. 46% [143/313]) or per intention to treat (ITT) at randomization (41.8% [138/330] vs. 43.5% [144/331]).
what_is_wrong: Nothing. Quote verbatim. The claim's load-bearing negative assertion - that this is a single-transfer endpoint and NOT a cumulative live birth rate - is independently supported: the word 'cumulative' appears exactly once in the entire STAR full text and refers to SART registry data ('final cumulative live birth rate per egg-retrieval cycle decreased from 54.5% ... to 13.4%'), never to STAR's own arms. STAR's ITT population is defined as 'patients undergoing randomization', with the numerator from one SET. My arithmetic: 41.82% vs 43.50%, RD -1.68pp, matching the claimed -1.7.

retrieval_method: parallel-cli extract of fertstert.org full text; Results paragraph, Statistical Analysis subsection, and Table 3 all read directly.
quote_found: A post hoc subgroup analysis revealed a higher OPR per transfer in women aged 35-40 years after PGT-A (50.8% vs. 37.2%; P=.035), but not in women aged 25-34 years (49.3% vs. 53.0%; P=.58). The OPRs were not significantly different between arms for women aged 25-34 years (42.5% vs. 50.3%; P=.17) or 35-40 years (41.1% vs. 35.7%; P=.35) when analyzed per ITT.
what_is_wrong: Nothing. I verified the three assertions SEPARATELY, as instructed. (1) POST HOC: the Statistical Analysis section states 'A post hoc analysis using the Fisher exact test was performed to evaluate clinical outcomes in two age populations: female ages 25-34 years and 35-40 years. Two age groups, 35-37 and 38-40 years, used during randomization were pooled for the post hoc analysis because of the small numbers in these groups.' - so the 35-40 band is a POOLING of two prespecified randomisation strata, created after the fact, exactly as the claim's note says. (2) PER-TRANSFER ONLY: Table 3 gives 62 (50.8) vs 54 (37.2) with 'P value for age subgroups P=.0349' under headers 'PGT-A (n = 122) |Control (n = 145)'; and 75 (49.3) vs 89 (53.0) under 'PGT-A (n = 152) |Control (n = 168)', P=.5757 - so the claimed counts 62/122, 54/145, 75/152, 89/168 are all correct. (3) VANISHES PER ITT: 41.1% vs 35.7%; P=.35, non-significant. The Discussion's '14%' figure the claim cites is also verbatim: 'demonstrated a significant improvement in OPR and live birth rate (14%) with the use of PGT-A per embryo transfer (51% [62/122[ vs. 37% [54/145]; P=.035)'. Sole caveat, and it is the claim's own framing not an error: per ITT the 35-40 point estimate still numerically favours PGT-A (41.1 vs 35.7), so 'did not persist' means lost significance, not reversed direction - the claim quotes both numbers so a reader cannot be misled.

retrieval_method: Europe PMC core record for EXT_ID:34818479 (N Engl J Med 2021;385(22):2047-2058), then parallel-cli extract --full-content of the NEJM full-text page (direct curl to NEJM is 403).
quote_found: All embryos that were obtained were cryopreserved and single frozen-embryo transfers were performed each time in the two groups.
what_is_wrong: Nothing. Quote verbatim in Methods/Procedures. Results verbatim: 'the primary outcome of cumulative live birth occurred in 468 of 606 women (77.2%) in the PGT-A group and in 496 of 606 (81.8%) in the conventional-IVF group (absolute difference, -4.6 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -9.2 to -0.0; P<0.001)'; Table 3 gives rate ratio 0.94 (0.89 to 1.00). Denominator checked as instructed: this is a genuine CUMULATIVE per-woman-randomised endpoint - 'The primary outcome was the cumulative live-birth rate after up to three embryo-transfer procedures within 1 year' and 'Only transfers of scheduled embryos (up to three in each group) that were performed within 1 year after randomization were included.' Population verbatim: 'A good prognosis was defined as a woman's age of 20 to 37 years and the availability of three or more good-quality blastocysts. A blastocyst was considered to be of good quality if the score according to the Gardner morphologic criteria on day 5 of embryo culture was 4BC or better.' The claim's per-protocol note also checks out verbatim: 'a live birth in 452 of 577 women (78.3%) in the PGT-A group and in 478 of 569 (84.0%) in the conventional-IVF group (absolute difference, -5.7 percentage points; 95% CI, -10.3 to -1.1)'. Both arms frozen, so the trial is correctly used for selection/discard and NOT for any fresh-vs-frozen inference.

retrieval_method: Same parallel-cli extract of the NEJM full text; Discussion paragraph read directly.
quote_found: We likewise found no significant differences between groups in the rates of ongoing pregnancy and live birth after the first frozen-embryo transfer. We also noted that the pregnancy outcomes after each of three transfers were all similar between the two groups when analyzed separately, whereas the cumulative pregnancy outcome was lower with PGT-A. These findings support the importance of the cumulative live-birth rate as the primary end point in clinical trials.
what_is_wrong: Nothing. Quote verbatim, in the Discussion. The corresponding Results sentence independently supports it: 'In the analyses of pregnancy outcomes performed separately for each embryo transfer, the proportions of women having a live birth, biochemical pregnancy, clinical pregnancy, ongoing pregnancy, and pregnancy loss were similar in the two groups for each outcome (Tables S2 through S5).' The claim deliberately records NO numerators/denominators because they sit in Tables S2-S5; I likewise could not open the supplementary appendix, and I regard the refusal to reconstruct them as correct practice rather than a gap. The claim's note figures are also verbatim: 'More women in the conventional-IVF group underwent a second or third embryo-transfer cycle: 192 women in the conventional-IVF group and 119 in the PGT-A group for a second cycle and 49 and 5, respectively, for a third cycle.'

retrieval_method: Europe PMC core record for EXT_ID:32898291 (Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2020, CD005291; PMC8094272 holds abstract only), then I downloaded the full review PDF myself with curl (HTTP 200, 981987 bytes) and ran pdftotext -layout over it. I read the forest-plot rows as TEXT from my own pdftotext output, not from the cached PNG.
quote_found: No studies reported on cLBR after blastocyst stage biopsy. It is uncertain if the addition of PGT-A with biopsy in the blastocyst stage improves LBR after the first embryo transfer or reduces the miscarriage rate.
what_is_wrong: Nothing. All three components verified. (1) Cumulative: 'Only one study provided cumulative live birth data (Verpoest 2018)' - polar body biopsy, OR 1.05 (0.66 to 1.66), N=396; there is no blastocyst subgroup in Analysis 1.1. (2) Forest plot row read verbatim from my own text extraction: '1.2.2 Blastocyst stage biopsy Munne 2019 (1) 138 330 144 331 100.0% 0.93 [0.69 , 1.27] Subtotal (95% CI) 330 331 100.0% 0.93 [0.69 , 1.27] Total events: 138 144 Heterogeneity: Not applicable Test for overall effect: Z = 0.44 (P = 0.66) Test for subgroup differences: Chi2 = 0.31, df = 1 (P = 0.58), I2 = 0%'. (3) Footnote verbatim: 'Footnotes (1) Freeze-all in both study arms only results of first single cryo embryo transfer'. Trivial orthography only: Cochrane spells the trial 'Munne 2019' with an acute accent on the e. The claim correctly scopes this to the genome-wide-analysis comparison and uses the freeze-all footnote as documentation of entanglement, not as evidence about freezing.

retrieval_method: Europe PMC core record for EXT_ID:36201787 (Obstet Gynecol 2022;140(5):769-777), then parallel-cli extract of the LWW/Green Journal abstract page via doi.org. Full text is closed: Unpaywall returns is_oa false / oa_status closed with zero OA locations, and the Semantic Scholar graph API returns isOpenAccess false with an empty openAccessPdf.
quote_found: A total of nine trials with 3,334 participants were included. Overall, PGT-A was not associated with an increased live-birth rate (RR 1.13, 95% CI 0.96-1.34, I2=79%). However, PGT-A raised the live-birth rate in women of advanced maternal age (RR 1.34, 95% CI 1.02-1.77, I2=50%) but not in women of nonadvanced age (RR 0.94, 95% CI 0.89-0.99, I2=0%).
what_is_wrong: Nothing in what is asserted; the numbers and the 'nine trials with 3,334 participants' are verbatim in the authors' structured abstract, and the effect estimates, CIs and all three I2 values match exactly. The claim is correctly limited to abstract-level evidence. I made an independent effort to break the maternal-age band (the failure mode named in my brief) and could NOT establish the numeric advanced-maternal-age cutoff, because the full text is paywalled by every open route I tried; the claim's own refusal to assert '35 years' is therefore the right call and should be preserved downstream. Likewise unresolved: whether the pooled live-birth RR is per woman randomised or per transfer. Note for the synthesis, not a defect in the claim: the paper's own stated Conclusion is more assertive than its Results ('Preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy increases the live-birth rate in women of advanced maternal age'), on I2=79% overall heterogeneity.
tried: doi.org -> journals.lww.com abstract page (succeeded, abstract only); Unpaywall API (is_oa false, no OA locations); Semantic Scholar graph API (openAccessPdf empty); parallel-cli web search for any accessible full text or the AMA definition (returned only unrelated general-audience pages defining advanced maternal age).

retrieval_method: Europe PMC core record for EXT_ID:28139240 (Fertil Steril 2017;107(3):723-730.e3), then parallel-cli extract --full-content of the fertstert.org full-text page; Tables 1-4 and Supplemental Tables 1-2 read directly.
quote_found: Freezing all embryos allows for inclusion of all blastocysts in the cohort of embryos available for transfer, which also results in a higher proportion of patients reaching ET.
what_is_wrong: The claim itself is fully confirmed: Table 2 (ITT) reads '|Live birth |35/88 (39.8) |56/91 (61.5) |<.01|' with headers 'Fresh ET (n = 88) |Frozen ET (n = 91)', Table 3 (per protocol) reads '|No. of live births (%/ET) |27/46 (59) |47/61 (77) |.04|', and the trial states 'Odds of a live birth was 2.1 (95% confidence interval 0.95-4.68; P=.68) with a frozen ET compared with a fresh ET.' Mean embryos transferred 1.4 fresh vs 1.5 frozen confirmed. The day-6 sentence is verbatim. ONE CORRECTION, to the claim's notes rather than to the claim: the notes say the ASRM 2024 opinion 'prints the adjusted OR P value as .68 which is inconsistent with the CI 0.95-4.68', implying an ASRM transcription error - in fact COATES 2017 ITSELF prints 'P=.68' next to that CI, and ASRM merely copied it, so the internal inconsistency belongs to the trial, not to ASRM. The notes' other two ASRM flags ARE correct and I verified both in my own copy of the ASRM PDF: ASRM prints 'ITT analysis demonstrated a significantly higher ongoing pregnancy rate (PR) (50.9% vs. 62.2%; p < 0.1) and live birth rate (LBR) (39.8 vs. 61.5%; p < 0.1)' where the trial reports ongoing PR '36/88 (40.9) vs 57/91 (62.6)' and P<.01. Also note the quoted sentence is verbatim only in the Abstract Conclusion(s), as the claim's location field states; the Discussion variant ends '...reaching their primary ET goal.' Finally, the claim is right that this is the only SQ4 design that varies freezing while holding biopsy constant.

retrieval_method: Europe PMC core record for EXT_ID:30689865 (Hum Reprod 2019;34(3):491-505); the academic.oup.com article URL failed with a network error in parallel-cli, so I re-extracted via doi.org, which returned 171 kB of full content including the Methods, Results, sensitivity analyses and the complete study-characteristics table.
quote_found: The study was categorised as having been performed in normal, high or poor responders based on the definition given by the authors of each eligible RCT.
what_is_wrong: The claim is confirmed, INCLUDING the data-integrity flag, which I verified from the paper itself as instructed. Verbatim: 'In high responders, a significantly higher probability of live birth was observed in the frozen ET group when compared with the fresh ET group (RR: 1.18, 95% CI: 1.06-1.31; fixed effects model; heterogeneity: I2 = 0%; three studies; n = 3398 patients)' and 'The probability of live birth was not significantly different ... in normal responders (RR: 1.13, 95% CI: 0.90-1.41; random effects model; heterogeneity: I2 = 77%; three studies; n = 1608 patients)'. From the study table I read the per-trial sizes: high responders Shapiro 2011b 122 + Absalan 2013 100 + Chen 2016 1508 + Aflatoonian 2018 280 = 2010; normal responders Shapiro 2011a 137 + Coates 2017 179 + Shi 2018 2157 + Vuong 2018 782 = 3255. The high-responder live-birth analysis names Absalan + Chen + Aflatoonian = 1888, so the printed n = 3398 is impossible. The normal-responder live-birth analysis names Coates + Shi + Vuong = 3118, and the paper's OWN sensitivity analysis proves the printed 1608 wrong from the inside: 'The exclusion of this study [Coates, n=179] resulted in no heterogeneity (I2 = 0%) between the remaining two RCTs (n = 2939 patients)' - and 2939 + 179 = 3118, not 1608. REFINEMENT to the claim's note: the two figures are not a simple transposition. 3398 = 179 + 2157 + 782 + 280, i.e. the three normal-responder trials plus Aflatoonian; and 1608 = 100 + 1508, i.e. Absalan plus Chen. So the error is a specific cross-wiring, not a swap of the two correct totals (1888 and 3118). The instruction 'Do NOT propagate n=3398' stands and should be strengthened to 'do not propagate n=1608 either'. The Absalan threshold quoted in the notes is also verbatim in the table: 'E2 >=3000 pg/ml on the day of hCG and >=15 follicles of 12-15 mm and >=16 mm'.

retrieval_method: Europe PMC core record for EXT_ID:27509101 (N Engl J Med 2016;375(6):523-533), then parallel-cli extract --full-content of the NEJM full-text page (I obtained the full article, not merely the PubMed abstract the claim relied on).
quote_found: Frozen-embryo transfer resulted in a higher frequency of live birth after the first transfer than did fresh-embryo transfer (49.3% vs. 42.0%), for a rate ratio of 1.17 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.05 to 1.31; P=0.004).
what_is_wrong: Nothing. Quote verbatim. Population verbatim: 'we randomly assigned 1508 infertile women with the polycystic ovary syndrome who were undergoing their first IVF cycle'; transfer policy verbatim: 'After 3 days of embryo development, women underwent the transfer of up to two fresh or frozen embryos'; preeclampsia verbatim: 'a higher frequency of preeclampsia (4.4% vs. 1.4%), for a rate ratio of 3.12 (95% CI, 1.26 to 7.73; P=0.009)'. The dominance argument is confirmed in Bosdou 2019 itself: 'In the one remaining paper, a significantly higher probability of live birth was observed in the frozen ET group when compared with the fresh ET group (RR: 1.17, 95% CI: 1.05-1.31; fixed effects model; heterogeneity: not applicable; one study; n = 1508 patients)', versus the pooled high-responder RR 1.18 (1.06-1.31). Bosdou's own characteristics table records Chen 2016's population as 'Women with PCOS' and its entry criterion as 'PCOS (Rotterdam criteria), first IVF cycle', while classifying it under 'High responders' - so the claim that the high-responder label here is inherited rather than oocyte-yield-based is exactly right.

retrieval_method: Europe PMC REST core record for EXT_ID:32964939, which carries the authors' complete structured abstract (Hum Reprod 2020;35(12):2808-2818, doi 10.1093/humrep/deaa226). The academic.oup.com full-text page failed with a network error in parallel-cli, so all verification is against the authors' own abstract text - which is where every number in the claim is sourced.
quote_found: The intention to treat clinical pregnancy and live birth rates (with the latter excluding four cases lost to follow-up: one in the fresh transfer and three in the freeze-all arms, respectively) after the first embryo transfer did not vary significantly among the fresh embryo transfer and freeze-all study arms: 51/105 (48.6%) versus 57/104 (54.8%) and 41/104 (39.4%) versus 42/101 (41.6%), respectively (relative risk for clinical pregnancy 1.13, 95% CI 0.87-1.47; P = 0.41).
what_is_wrong: Nothing. Quote verbatim, and every subsidiary element checks out against the same abstract. Threshold verbatim: 'women with an excessive response to ovarian stimulation (>=18 follicles measuring >=11 mm) undergoing IVF/ICSI in a GnRH antagonist suppressed cycle' - a follicle-count criterion, not oocyte yield and not PCOS, as the claim says. Randomisation verbatim: 'A total of 212 patients (106 in each arm) were recruited'. OHSS verbatim: 'moderate-to-severe OHSS occurred solely in the group that received low-dose hCG (9/105, 8.6%, 95% CI 3.2% to 13.9% vs 0/104, 95% CI 0 to 3.7, P < 0.01)' - and the low-dose-hCG group IS the fresh-transfer arm ('a fresh embryo transfer with intensified luteal phase support (1500 IU hCG on the day of oocyte retrieval ...)'), so the claim's phrasing 'only in the fresh-transfer arm' is correct. Power caveat verbatim: 'The sample size calculation was based on a 19% absolute difference in terms of clinical pregnancy rates'. My arithmetic reproduces +2.2pp for live birth and +6.2pp for clinical pregnancy.
tried: academic.oup.com/humrep/article/35/12/2808/5910108 via parallel-cli extract (network_error); Europe PMC core record (succeeded, full structured abstract). Full text not needed because the claim sources every figure from the abstract.

retrieval_method: I retrieved the primary document twice, myself, and did not open figs_source/asrm_pgta_2024.pdf. (1) curl of the asrm.org PDF (HTTP 200, 319904 bytes, 28 pages) then pdftotext in both -raw and -layout modes. (2) curl of the asrm.org practice-document landing page, which carries the entire committee opinion inline as HTML. Europe PMC core record for EXT_ID:38762806 independently confirms Fertil Steril 2024;122(3):421-434.
quote_found: At present, however, the routine use of blastocyst biopsy with aneuploidy testing in all infertile patients undergoing IVF treatment cannot be recommended.
what_is_wrong: The QUOTATION IS WORD-FOR-WORD ACCURATE in both of my independent copies, and the claim body is accurate, so the verdict is CONFIRMED. Metadata all check out: byline on page 1 of the PDF reads 'Practice Committees of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine and the Society for Assisted Reproductive Technology'; citation line reads 'Fertil Steril 2024;122: 421-34'; and 'This document replaces the document of the same name, last published in 2018.' TWO LOCATION ERRORS to fix before publication, neither affecting the wording: (a) the sentence is the FINAL SENTENCE OF THE 'CONCLUSIONS' SECTION, not of 'Patient Priorities and Individual Consideration' - I mapped the all-caps headings and the sentence sits at a text offset after 'CONCLUSIONS' and immediately before 'Acknowledgments', with 'PATIENT PRIORITIES AND INDIVIDUAL CONSIDERATION' being the preceding section; (b) it is on journal page 430, not 429 - PDF page 10 carries the running footer '430 VOL. 122 NO. 3 / SEPTEMBER 2024' and contains both headings and the sentence, while page 429 ends before them. The two supplementary sentences in the claim's notes are also verbatim: 'The value of PGT-A as a universal screening test for all patients undergoing IVF has not been demonstrated.' (Conclusions) and 'The value of PGT-A as a routine screening test for all patients undergoing in vitro fertilization has not been demonstrated.' (abstract).

retrieval_method: Same two independent copies I downloaded myself (asrm.org PDF via curl + pdftotext -raw; asrm.org landing page HTML via curl). Sentence located in both.
quote_found: Potential risks of a ‘‘freeze-all’’ strategy include increased risk of maternal hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and having a large-for-gestational-age infant (47).
what_is_wrong: Nothing. THE QUOTATION IS WORD-FOR-WORD ACCURATE, including the reference callout (47) and the document's doubled-single-quote rendering of ‘‘freeze-all’’. The location is also correct: it is the last sentence of the 'FROZEN EMBRYO TRANSFER CYCLES' section and is immediately followed by the heading 'DAY OF EMBRYO BIOPSY'. The second limb of the claim - that ASRM frames the pivotal PGT-A RCTs as frozen-transfer trials - is verbatim in the Conclusions: 'However, 2 recent, multicenter, randomized control trials in women with available blastocysts concluded that overall pregnancy outcomes via FET were similar between conventional IVF vs. PGT-A.', and in the abstract: 'recent multicenter, randomized control trials in women with available blastocysts concluded that the overall pregnancy outcomes via frozen embryo transfer were similar between PGT-A and conventional in vitro fertilization.' I also independently mapped all 18 all-caps section headings of the document and found no standalone section on elective freeze-all, which supports the claim's retrieval finding that this sentence is the nearest thing to an ASRM position on the topic.

retrieval_method: Deliberately independent of the first agent's NCBI eutils route and of figs_source/eshre_addons_2023.xml. I used the Europe PMC REST full-text XML endpoint (628542 bytes; note the /PMC/PMC.../ form 404s, the bare /PMC.../ form works), stripped tags myself, and then CROSS-CHECKED every sentence against a second copy I fetched separately from pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10628516/ (769257 bytes of HTML). Both copies contain the sentences character-for-character. Europe PMC core record confirms Hum Reprod 2023;38(11):2062-2104, doi 10.1093/humrep/dead184, 'ESHRE Add-ons working group, Lundin K, Bentzen JG, ... Vermeulen N, Pinborg A.'
quote_found: Elective freeze-all is currently not recommended for routine clinical use.
what_is_wrong: Nothing. THE QUOTATION IS WORD-FOR-WORD ACCURATE. Location confirmed by section mapping: the sentence closes the 'Recommendation' subsection of the 'Elective freeze-all' section and is immediately followed by the heading 'ICSI for non-male factor infertility'; it also appears identically in the summary table. The companion sentence in the claim's notes is likewise verbatim: 'The freeze-all strategy should only be considered when there is a clear clinical indication, such as a higher risk of OHSS or endometrial pathology, and in cases involving PGT.' - so the claim's paraphrase ('higher OHSS risk, endometrial pathology, or PGT') is faithful. The scoping caveat is verbatim too: 'For the aim of this article, freeze-all in the context of women with PCOS or preventing OHSS was not evaluated as this is not considered an add-on.' Both mis-transcription warnings in the notes are CORRECT and I verified them in my own copy: ESHRE writes 'a significantly higher probability of live birth was present in high, but not normal responders ... (RR 1.13; 95% CI 0.90 to 1.41; 3 RCT; n = 3118) (Bosdou etal., 2019)', which attaches Bosdou's NON-significant normal-responder estimate to the high-responder claim; and its Table 3 renders Yan 2021 as '458/606 (77.2%) vs 496/606 (81.8%)' where NEJM reports 468/606 (458/606 is 75.6%, so it is internally inconsistent as well). I add a third ESHRE error the claim did not catch: ESHRE states 'The meta-analysis included 3398 women, in which the RCT from China on women with PCOS accounted for more than 3000 patients (Chen etal., 2016)' - Chen 2016 randomised 1508, not more than 3000. The instruction not to source trial numbers from this document should be kept.

retrieval_method: Same two independent copies as SQ4-C14 (Europe PMC REST full-text XML, cross-checked against the pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov HTML I fetched separately).
quote_found: Pre-implantation genetic testing for aneuploidy is currently not recommended for routine clinical use.
what_is_wrong: Nothing substantive. THE QUOTATION IS WORD-FOR-WORD ACCURATE, including the hyphen in 'Pre-implantation'. I checked the unhyphenated variant 'Preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy is currently not recommended' and it returns ZERO hits in the document, so the hyphen must be preserved if the sentence is quoted; the claim's quote field has it right, though the claim's own prose sentence and its location field render the section title unhyphenated where ESHRE writes 'Pre-implantation genetic testing for aneuploidy'. Location confirmed: the sentence closes the 'Recommendation' subsection of that section and is immediately followed by 'Non-invasive pre-implantation genetic testing'. The second limb of the claim is verbatim: 'Because of the introduction of blastocyst biopsy in conjunction with shallow sequencing, freeze-all of biopsied embryos is mostly applied in these cycles. This brings its own risks, as discussed in the paragraph on the freeze-all strategy.' So is the age-band caution quoted in the notes: 'The supposition that PGT-A reduces miscarriages or time-to-pregnancy in specific patient groups, such as those with advanced maternal age, is based on post hoc analyses (Munne etal., 2019) and requires further investigation to establish its validity.' (ESHRE prints Munne with an acute accent).
